sources.entry: LimeSurvey - Feature-rich web-based polling software. Supports extensive survey logic. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-2.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: LimeSurvey is a free, open-source, web-based survey platform for building and running online surveys with conditional logic, branching, and multilingual support.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes LimeSurvey as a web-based survey platform offering conditional logic, skip logic and question branching, and customizable templates. It lists 30+ question types, multilingual surveys (80+ languages), and survey sharing via public link, QR code, or closed invite-only access via personal link. Responses, statistics, and data analysis tools are included, along with on-brand styling (fonts, colors, logo, CSS, JavaScript). It names a RemoteControl API (XML-RPC / JSON-RPC), two-factor authentication, data anonymization, and plugins and integrations such as SAML, LDAP, and REST API. The README also states GDPR compliance and WCAG 2.0 compliance.
use_cases: Running customer or employee feedback surveys
Conducting academic research or field studies
Building multilingual surveys for global audiences
Creating surveys with skip logic and branching
Self-hosting a survey platform instead of a SaaS tool
how_to_run: Download the latest stable release from the project's download channel (the README links to it; no exact commands given)
Install on a PHP-capable web server (Apache 2.4+, nginx 1.1+, or similar)
Provide PHP 8.1.29+ with mbstring and PDO drivers
Provide a supported database: MySQL 8.0+, PostgreSQL 14+, MariaDB 10.3.38+, or MSSQL 2019+
Optionally use the recommended stack: nginx, php-fpm, MariaDB or MySQL
notable: Conditional logic, question branching, and skip logic for complex survey flows
RemoteControl API via XML-RPC and JSON-RPC
Plugin ecosystem including audit log, ExportR, ExportSTATAxml, and AuthCAS
Integrations named in README: SAML, LDAP, SURFconext, REST API
Hosted SaaS option offered by the vendor for users who don't want to self-host
caveats: Self-hosting requires a PHP stack and a supported database server
README promotes a paid-or-hosted SaaS option; self-hosting setup details are not in the README
Development repository may contain versions that are not fully tested; stable release is recommended
summary.license: GPL-2.0 (GPL v2.0, with option to use any later GPL version)
